functional_evidence: Private predecessors are filtered before history differences are calculated.
Only managers receive aggregate binding counts; no personal account or credential information is published.
Missing stop confirmation is rejected; changed binding counts return 409 and require another confirmation.
Six concurrent bind/stop scenarios produce only a confirmed stop without a new binding, or a new binding with the stop rejected.
Old revisions can be stopped and reenabled independently while other revisions remain available.
Real native and JDBC PostgreSQL failures cover authentication, database absence, refused network connection and TLS refusal.
Real native and JDBC MySQL failures distinguish authentication from permission denial; an inaccessible missing database is reported as permission denial rather than guessed absence.
Typed unit cases also cover Redis error prefixes, DNS, certificates, timeout, capacity, service authentication and unknown causes.
Mobile credential repair focuses an empty personal password field, verifies the real database login and clears stale failure data.
Desktop and portrait mobile revision dialog pagination remains inside the viewport.
limits: GaussDB real-service validation, organization tenancy and targeted user-group publishing are outside this change.
Stop-impact confirmation is based on the current count of saved personal connections, not active sessions or cancellation of already admitted operations.
Unknown connection causes remain unknown; classification does not prove a database exists or an account has all required privileges.
Native 12-version matrix and standalone production JDBC image/TLS suites were not rerun. Java compilation, typed cause checks and live JDBC HTTP integrations were run on the changed source.
No main merge or production deployment.
